scope: All 242 legacy Testimonials Showcase (ttshowcase) records, read-only audit. No legacy post, meta, term or media was modified.

lookup_policy.matched: The review was located on the stated third-party platform and its identity confirmed against the stored record.
lookup_policy.not-found: A lookup was performed and no matching third-party review exists. For a record whose sct_source is direct this means no third-party platform record exists at all, because the testimonial was collected directly.
lookup_policy.blocked: A lookup was attempted and the platform refused the request or returned no readable content, so the outcome is unknown and is never guessed.

source_rules.google: sct_source is google only where the legacy record stores _rsp_google_review_id. That key is written by the Google Business Profile capture workflow rather than by an editor typing a platform name, so it is first-party evidence. Two records qualify: 88416 and 88417.
source_rules.direct: Every other legacy record stores no third-party platform identifier of any kind. sct_source is direct, which renders no third-party attribution instead of claiming a platform that cannot be evidenced.
source_rules.rejected_evidence: Platform words appearing inside quote text or inside the legacy _aditional_info_url client-link field were reviewed one by one and rejected as source evidence. In every case the sentence describes how the client found the photographer, or is a link to the client's own post, not a statement of where the client published the review. Counting those as source would be guessing.

platforms.reason: Confirmed through Ryan's own signed-in Google account in Chrome. Both reviewer contributor pages list a review of Ryan Smith Photography at 151 Empyrean Cir, Myrtle Beach, SC 29588 whose visible text is a character-for-character prefix of the quote stored on the legacy record.
evidence: Signed-in session, https://www.google.com/maps/contrib/110067136242588282743/reviews shows reviewer Jessica Fram, Local Guide Level 4, 16 reviews, including Ryan Smith Photography, 151 Empyrean Cir, Myrtle Beach, SC 29588, posted a week ago

Google visible text for that review: We met Ryan at the Bridal Expo and fell in love with his photos! He did not disappoint the day of our wedding. He gave me the option to send photos that I wanted to replicate. He also had great ideas for around the venue, as well as on the ... which is a verbatim prefix of the quote stored on legacy record 88416; Google truncates the remainder behind a More control

Signed-in session, https://www.google.com/maps/contrib/111381239245316784506/reviews shows reviewer Emily Kauff, Local Guide Level 2, 2 reviews and 3 ratings, including Ryan Smith Photography, 151 Empyrean Cir, Myrtle Beach, SC 29588, posted 11 hours ago

Google visible text for that review: I absolutely love how our family picture turned out, Ryan was very outgoing and easy to work with, also very understanding that 2 3year olds and a ornery 7 year old were not really interested in taking pictures as much as the teenager girls ... which is a verbatim prefix of the quote stored on legacy record 88417

Distinctive phrase needles confirmed present in the signed-in page text: Bridal Expo, He did not disappoint, ornery, family picture. The phrases sneak peak and random questions were absent only because they fall after Google's More truncation, not because the text differs
Confirmation timestamp 2026-10-02T04:06:28Z, performed in Ryan's own signed-in Chrome profile

Anonymous HTTP attempts against the same seven Google endpoints at 2026-10-02T03:54:51Z returned 404s or JavaScript shells with anti-bot markers and zero needle hits, which is why a signed-in browser was required
platforms.note: sct_source is google because both legacy records store _rsp_google_review_id together with a Maps contributor profile URL. sct_source_lookup is matched because the signed-in confirmation located both reviews on Google and matched their visible text verbatim.

platforms.reason: No third-party platform identifier is stored on these records, so there is no external record to reconcile against. not-found states that plainly rather than implying a platform was searched and came up empty by accident.
